transcript: If you're an overthinker, I know exactly what your problem is. When you start getting attached to someone, your emotional state slowly begins to depend on how they respond to you. A short reply can make you anxious. A change in tone can ruin your day. Silence feels personal even when it isn't. You're not imagining this. You're highly sensitive to emotional shifts. You notice energy, patterns, and small changes that most people completely miss. The problem is not that you feel deeply. The problem is that your nervous system starts outsourcing safety to another person. So when their mood changes, your body reacts as if something is wrong. Your mind fills the gap with stories. You replay conversations. You try to fix things that were never broken. Here's the solution. You have to bring your emotional center back into your own body. Instead of asking, why are they acting different, ask, what am I feeling right now and what do I need? Slow your breath. Feel your feet on the ground. Remind your nervous system. I am safe even without reassurance. Attachment becomes unhealthy when someone else becomes the regulator of your emotions. Healing begins when you learn to self-soothe before seeking connection. Connection should add to your peace, not decide it. And the moment you stop chasing emotional certainty from others, your mind quiets, your anxiety softens, and relationships become lighter, not heavier. If this feels familiar, comment stillness below. And if you want to go deeper, my new ebook, The Way Back to Stillness, is in the link on my profile.
